title: Affiliate Disclosure
description: How Deal Notes earns money from Amazon affiliate links, why we do not show Amazon prices or star ratings, and how picks are chosen.
intro: Deal Notes earns money through affiliate links. As an Amazon Associate, Deal Notes earns from qualifying purchases.

sections.answer: A link that tells the store which site sent you. If you buy something after clicking, the store may pay us a small commission. Your price is the same.
body: Links to Amazon on this site are marked as sponsored in the page code, and every page shows a short disclosure near the top.

sections.h: Do commissions affect which products you recommend?
sections.answer: No. Picks come from published, test-based reviews and maker specs, as each guide's "How we chose" section explains. We include products whether or not they pay a commission.

sections.h: Why don't you show Amazon prices or ratings?
sections.answer: Amazon's rules only allow affiliate sites to show live prices and similar product data through its official Product Advertising API, which becomes available after a site makes qualifying sales. Copying prices or star ratings by hand can be out of date and is not allowed.
body: So we use "Check price on Amazon" buttons that open the current listing. We also never show fake countdown timers or invented ratings.

sections.h: Are there other affiliate programs or ads?
sections.answer: Not today. If we add other affiliate programs or display ads, we will list them here and in our privacy policy.
